subject.title: feat(plugin-sdk): generic outbound delivery-report seam; WhatsApp native auto-reply reports provider-accepted sends

question: Should OpenClaw accept `openclaw/plugin-sdk/outbound-delivery-report` as the public generic contract for self-delivered channel sends, with the idempotency and fail-open semantics in this PR?
rationale: The code path is plausible, but the exact SDK surface becomes a compatibility contract once released and automation should not choose that API direction without maintainer intent.

options.title: Accept after proof
options.body: Require redacted real WhatsApp/runtime proof, then accept this generic seam as the supported contract.

options.title: Revise API shape first
options.body: Keep the branch open but ask for a maintainer-selected name, payload shape, or idempotency policy before merge.

options.title: Keep slice-specific fixes
options.body: Reject the public generic seam for now and handle native self-delivery hook coverage through channel-specific emitters or a broader design issue.

recommendation.title: Accept after proof
recommendation.body: Require redacted real WhatsApp/runtime proof, then accept this generic seam as the supported contract.
